final.memo:
Our investment in CoStar remains anchored by the unique quality of its commercial real estate information franchise, which remains the 'Bloomberg' of its asset class [D01]. The central event-driven catalyst—the April 2025 governance settlement—is currently in the implementation phase [D03, D07]. By placing John Berisford, Rachel Glaser, and Christine McCarthy on the board, we have secured a mechanism to oversee capital allocation and compensation, directly addressing our concerns regarding historical empire-building [D03, D07].

The fundamental underwriting challenge is separating this high-margin, recurring commercial business from the cash-intensive, loss-making residential strategy [D02, D06]. The bears argue that Homes.com investment will continue to consume commercial profits indefinitely, rendering the governance remedy toothless [D05]. Our objective is to test this against actual operating disclosures rather than management rhetoric; we require empirical evidence of disciplined spending and improved cash conversion [D02, D03, D05].

We are in a holding pattern while the new directors establish their oversight. We do not have sufficient visibility into the precise segment-level cash bridge to justify an immediate exit or a significant increase in exposure [D02, D04]. We will monitor core commercial earnings and Homes.com investment levels closely as they are the primary metrics for determining whether this management team can deliver on the implied efficiency gains [D01, D07]. As we are now a party to the board agreement, we maintain our position while the agreed-upon plan proceeds [D03].
